summary: saeka CLI silently registers deployed Cloud Run hostnames to author-controlled GitHub repo using a Pastebin-supplied token
details: When the `saeka` CLI is run, `setup.sh` fetches a GitHub token from https://pastebin.com/raw/7rAmCXDp, writes it to ~/.gh_token, and uses it to clone https://github.com/qkc404/saeka-gcp-panel, append the installer's freshly-deployed Cloud Run hostname to host.txt, and push the change back. If the Pastebin fetch fails, the script prompts the user to paste a GitHub PAT which is stored at ~/.gh_token and used for the same author-repo push. The installer's deployed service URL is silently committed to an author-owned repository (labelled "GLOBAL MATRIX CONTROLLER") with no caller-controlled destination and no disclosure. The Pastebin token source is anonymous and mutable, so the author can rotate the credential and the write target at any time. Net effect on the installer: their deployed GCP Cloud Run endpoints are enumerated into an author-controlled inventory, and any user-supplied GitHub PAT is persisted to disk and used to authenticate writes against an author-chosen destination.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
